title: 171 Interrelationships of subjectively and objectively evaluated conformational phenotypes in mature beef cows as it relates to energetic efficiency during a 42 day reconditioning phase
content:
Abstract
The objective of this experiment was toinvestigate how phenotypic measurements independent of body weight affect maintenance energy and efficiency of mature beef cows. A total of 81 crossbred commercial cows were selected from a subset of 200 head. The experiment utilized a 3x3 factorial arrangement of treatments with frame score (small, medium, and large) and body capacity, (shallow, moderate, and deep) serving as main effects (9 cows/trmt; 27 cows/main effect). Growth and intake data were analyzed as a nested analysis of variance with frame and body serving as blocking factors using SPSS Statistics 25.0 (IBM, Armonk, NY). Pearson’s correlation analysis was performed to assess relationships of phenotypic measurements. Cattle were all placed on a maintenance ration and evaluated on daily intakes using feed intake nodes (SmartFeed Pro, C-Lock, Rapid City, SD). Every 14 days (d 0, 14, 28, and 42), cows were be weighed, ultrasounded by a UGC certified carcass technician (FT, rump fat, REA, and IMF), imaged to create a 3-dimensional body conformation configuration using millimeter radar technology (SizeR, Geissler Corporation), and subjectively scored by a trained 3 person panel for BCS (1 to 9), body capacity (1 to 9), frame score (1 to 9), and structural soundness (1 to 9). No evidence that phenotypic metrics affected ADG (P = 0.182), DMI (P = 0.179), or change in BCS from d0 to d42 (P = 0.078). In conclusion, although data represented no significant differences, numeric differences indicate that furth research is necessary to investigate phenotypic variation further.
